name: es30-glsl-texture-functions
title: GLSL ES 3.00 texture lookup and derivative functions
summary: Every GLSL ES 3.00 §8.8 lookup form (texture with and without bias, textureProj, textureLod, textureOffset, textureLodOffset, textureGrad, textureGradOffset, textureProjLod, textureProjOffset, textureProjLodOffset, textureProjGrad, textureProjGradOffset, texelFetch, texelFetchOffset, textureSize) on sampler2D, sampler3D, sampler2DArray, samplerCube, usampler2D, isampler3D, usamplerCube and the three shadow samplers, in the fragment stage (RGBA32UI target) and the vertex stage (transform feedback), compared texel by texel with a CPU model of ES 3.0 level selection, with a negative control per case; dFdx / dFdy / fwidth of affine functions; compile-time rules of the lookup functions.
spec: GLSL ES 3.00 §8.8 Texture Lookup Functions, §8.9 Fragment Processing Functions
GLSL ES 3.00 §4.5.4 Default Precision Qualifiers (sampler types without a default precision)
ES 3.0 §2.12.9.2 Texel Fetches, §2.12.9.3 Texture Size Query, §2.12.9.4 Texture Access (vertex stage: lambda_base = lod or 0)
ES 3.0 §3.8.9 Cube Map Texture Selection (Table 3.21), §3.8.9.1 Seamless Cube Map Filtering (NEAREST clamps to the edge)

ES 3.0 §3.8.10.1 Scale Factor and Level of Detail (equations 3.16-3.20, bias clamp, approximation bounds of rho), §3.8.10.2 Coordinate Wrapping and Texel Selection (Table 3.22, array layer rounding), §3.8.10.4 Mipmapping (equation 3.23)
ES 3.0 §3.8.13 Texture Completeness (non-filterable integer and depth formats with NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST)
ES 3.0 §3.8.15.1 Depth Texture Comparison Mode (Table 3.23 LEQUAL)

api.glGenTextures: ten lookup textures and the RGBA32UI result texture; every lookup result names its texture's texels
api.glActiveTexture: units 0-9 hold the ten sampler kinds, unit 10 the result texture; each sampler uniform reads its own texture (checked through the encoded texels)
api.glBindTexture: 2D, 3D, 2D array and cube targets; the per-texel encodings come back through the lookups
api.glTexImage2D: every level of the RGBA8 / RGBA32UI 2D and DEPTH_COMPONENT32F 2D textures and of all six faces of the RGBA8 / RGBA8UI / DEPTH_COMPONENT32F cube maps; each texel read back through texelFetch / texture* and compared with its encoded address
api.glTexImage3D: every level of the RGBA8 3D, RGBA32I 3D, RGBA8 2D array and DEPTH_COMPONENT32F 2D array textures (depth halves only for 3D); verified through lookups and textureSize
api.glTexParameteri: NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST / NEAREST, REPEAT vs CLAMP_TO_EDGE (offsets that wrap or clamp are compared with the Table 3.22 model), COMPARE_REF_TO_TEXTURE with LEQUAL (shadow result pairs); set through the typed glTexParameter overloads
api.glGetIntegerv: MIN/MAX_PROGRAM_TEXEL_OFFSET checked against Table 6.32 and compiled into the textureOffset limit case; MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS
api.glGetFloatv: MAX_TEXTURE_LOD_BIAS checked against Table 6.28 and used by the model of the clamped bias
api.glBindFramebuffer: probe target for the lookups, default framebuffer for the picture; both read back
api.glFramebufferTexture2D: RGBA32UI texture level 0 as COLOR_ATTACHMENT0; completeness checked, results read back
api.glCheckFramebufferStatus: the RGBA32UI target must be FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE
api.glScissor: one 4x4 block per lookup; every block holds its own case (a leaking draw would break the neighbouring block's comparison)
api.glReadPixels: RGBA_INTEGER / UNSIGNED_INT readback of the 128x64 RGBA32UI target (raw float bits and integers); RGBA / UNSIGNED_BYTE probes of the picture
api.glDrawArrays: one triangle per fragment-stage lookup, 13 points for the vertex-stage lookups, the plane and the result cells
api.glUseProgram: six probe programs (one per sampler family), the transform-feedback program and the two picture programs
api.glGetUniformLocation: case selector, coordinates, gradients, lod, fetch coordinates, depth references, sampler units
api.glUniform1i: case selector (selects the lookup that is compared) and the sampler units
api.glUniform1f: explicit lod or bias of each case; the levels chosen are compared
api.glUniform2f: block origin; the coordinates depend on it
api.glUniform4f: P, dP/dx, dP/dy and the explicit gradients of each case
api.glUniform4i: texelFetch coordinate and lod, textureSize sampler and lod
api.glUniform2fv: u_ref[16] depth references per pixel (shadow cases) and u_vref[13] (vertex stage)
api.glUniform4fv: u_vp[13] vertex-stage coordinates indexed by gl_VertexID
api.glUniform2i: the result block a picture cell shows (probed in the picture)
api.glTransformFeedbackVaryings: flat uvec4 v_result captured (INTERLEAVED_ATTRIBS) and compared per vertex
api.glGenTransformFeedbacks: transform feedback object holding the capture binding
api.glBindTransformFeedback: capture into the bound object's buffer
api.glBindBufferBase: TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_BUFFER binding 0; the captured values are read back
api.glBeginTransformFeedback: POINTS capture of the 13 vertex-stage lookups
api.glMapBufferRange: MAP_READ_BIT read of the captured lookup results
api.glEnable: SCISSOR_TEST per block, RASTERIZER_DISCARD during the capture
api.glGenVertexArrays: attribute-less VAO for the gl_VertexID-generated geometry
api.glCreateShader: lookup shaders and the ten compile-rule shaders (via demo::compile_shader)
api.glCompileShader: five lookup-rule violations must fail, their five positive controls must compile
api.glAttachShader: vertex + fragment shader of the transform-feedback program
api.glDeleteShader: rule shaders and the transform-feedback shaders
api.glViewport: probe target, picture regions and cells sized from the window

visual_review.notes: Viewed the CTest gpu es-max capture (256x256) and own radeonsi captures at 800x800, 640x480 and 333x777 (portrait: plane on top, grid below). Left (top) part: a ground plane in perspective whose implicit-LOD texture() bands run red (level 0) near the camera through orange, yellow, green and cyan to blue at the far edge, with a fine texel-parity checker; a thin dark sky strip at the very top. Right (bottom) part: 154 framed cells filling the rest of the window: palette-coloured lookup cells (solid level colours, two-tone stripes where the block spans two texels, checkerboards for the per-pixel texel changes), a run of green shadow cells (result pair (1, 0)), the textureSize cells (bright yellow for the 32x16 level 0, darkening with the level) and the six derivative cells at the end (brown, dark red, orange-red, near-black, dark teal, and white for the large dFdx(x^2) values). Picture fills the window at every size; 100x100 reports SKIP_UNSUPPORTED.
